h1:
Where to Stay in Chonburi & Pattaya?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 12 hand-picked Chonburi & Pattaya hotels across every budget — from 5-star sea-view towers in the city centre down to hostels a 3-minute walk from the beach. Covering the main areas: Pattaya, Jomtien–Na Jomtien, Naklua–Wong Amat and Bangsaen. From roughly ฿280–4,800/night.
introH2: 🏖️ Why does choosing the right area in Chonburi & Pattaya matter so much?
introHtml: Chonburi isn't just Pattaya, and Pattaya isn't just Walking Street — each area has a completely different vibe. Central Pattaya is the hub of convenience: next to the malls and the beach, but buzzing day and night. Naklua–Wong Amat on the north side is quieter and cleaner, ideal for family resorts. Jomtien–Na Jomtien to the south is the calm-beach zone with clearer water, made for relaxing. And Bangsaen, in Chonburi city itself, is the sea nearest Bangkok — perfect for a weekend road trip. Many people book without checking the area, then lose hours shuttling back and forth. This guide rounds up 12 Chonburi & Pattaya hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — from sea-view luxury down to hostels you can walk to the beach from — each with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Chonburi & Pattaya have no metro. Getting around means songthaew (red baht-bus) in Pattaya, Grab, or your own car. From Bangkok it's about 1.5–2 hours to Pattaya and around 1.5 hours to Bangsaen. U-Tapao Airport (UTP) is about 45 min from Pattaya. The areas in this guide: Central Pattaya — Beach Road, CentralFestival, Walking Street · Naklua–Wong Amat — north Pattaya, quieter, beachfront resorts · Jomtien–Na Jomtien — calm beaches, clear water · Bangsaen — Chonburi city, the sea closest to Bangkok, near Burapha University and Nong Mon Market.

entries.name: Hilton Pattaya
entries.badge: 🏆 Luxury · sea view in every room
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Beach Road · above CentralFestival · walk to beach
entries.addr: 333/101 Moo 9, Beach Road, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung, Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: Scoring 9.1 from 2,223 reviews — Hilton Pattaya is a luxury hotel on a 34-storey tower above CentralFestival mall on Beach Road, where all 303 rooms look out over a 180-degree sweep of Pattaya Bay, each with a private balcony. The highlights are the 16th-floor infinity pool and the Horizon Rooftop bar for cocktails at sunset. You step out of the lift into the mall and the beach, then back up to a room floating above the noise — ideal for travellers who want city-centre convenience without losing the sea view.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a high floor on the side away from Beach Road for quiet and a wider view. The upgrade to an Executive room is modest but gets you the Executive Lounge with free afternoon tea and evening canapés — worth it if you like to lounge.
pros: 180-degree Pattaya Bay views from every room, with a private balcony
Connected to CentralFestival — lift down to restaurants and the beach
Floating infinity pool and Horizon Rooftop bar, great atmosphere
Attentive, polite staff and spacious 46 sqm rooms, renovated 2020
cons: Rooms facing Beach Road catch traffic and nightlife noise
Not a private-sand resort, and in-hotel food and drink prices are high

entries.name: Centara Grand Mirage Beach Resort Pattaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wong Amat Beach · North Pattaya · beachfront
entries.storyHtml: The most-reviewed property in this guide — over 7,862 reviews — Centara Grand Mirage is a 5-star resort with its own Lost World-themed waterpark on Wong Amat Beach in North Pattaya. There are waterfalls, caves, slides, a lazy river and four pools, so kids can play all day without leaving. With 555 sea-view rooms, a kids' club and five restaurants, it's the most talked-about family resort in Pattaya — though it gets crowded in peak season and in-resort prices run high.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Request the Mirage Wing for newer rooms and a clearer sea view. Hit the waterpark early before the crowds and reserve a poolside lounger. Eating out at Terminal 21 or Naklua Market is much cheaper than in the resort.
pros: In-house waterpark — kids play all day, great for families
On Wong Amat Beach, the quieter, cleaner North Pattaya side
Spacious sea-view rooms with private balconies on almost all units
Kids' club, 4 pools and 5 restaurants — everything in one place
cons: Very busy in peak season; waterpark packed, loungers hard to grab
High in-resort food and drink prices; not for couples seeking quiet

entries.name: Rabbit Resort Pattaya
tags: 🌳 Thai village in a tropical garden
entries.addr: 318/84 Moo 12, Soi Dongtan, Thappraya Road, Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: The top score in this guide at 9.4 (TripAdvisor 4.8/5, ranked #15 of 619 Pattaya hotels) — Rabbit Resort is a Thai village set in a tropical garden of more than 4 hectares, right on Dongtan Beach. Just 49 timber cottages and villas in Thai style are scattered under mature trees, with a main house around 100 years old. There are two pools (one reserved for adults) and you can walk straight from the garden onto the sand. The freshly made breakfast draws constant praise — ideal for couples who want calm and Thai character right by the beach.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a cottage deeper in the garden for more quiet and greenery. Couples should use the adults-only pool. Don't miss the freshly made breakfast and the resort's own bakery.
pros: Top score in the guide 9.4 · serene tropical-garden setting
Directly on Dongtan Beach, quieter and cleaner than the main Pattaya beach
Spacious, very clean rooms with distinctive Thai-antique decor
Quiet adults-only pool for couples · freshly made breakfast praised
cons: Pricey for a 4-star in Pattaya (you pay for the atmosphere)
The antique style may not suit travellers who prefer modern, minimal rooms

entries.name: The Standard, Pattaya Na Jomtien
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Na Jomtien Beach · ~20 min from central Pattaya
entries.addr: 8/12 Moo 2, Na Jomtien Soi 10, Na Jomtien, Sattahip, Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: Scoring 9.2 — The Standard, Pattaya Na Jomtien is a design hotel that opened in 2025 and breaks the mould completely. The curving modernist architecture by ONION is paired with bold 1960s colour, so every corner is photogenic. It's the first beach club in The Standard chain, with the Mexican-style Esmé, a seafront pool, a private beach and an evening DJ. The rooms are brand new and spotless. The hotel is a destination in itself — though the team is still finding its feet and it's about 20–25 min from central Pattaya.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Booking 14 days ahead usually gets a better rate. Ask for a high-floor sea-view room to catch the Na Jomtien sunset. If you plan to go into Pattaya, schedule your rides — it's 20–25 min away.
pros: Bold 1960s design with real character — photogenic everywhere
On Na Jomtien Beach, clear water, calm vibe and a lovely sunset
Esmé beach club and seafront pool with an evening DJ
Brand-new, very clean, spacious rooms (opened 2025)
cons: About 20–25 min from central Pattaya — you'll need a ride to go in
Newly opened, so some service is still inconsistent and check-in can be slow

entries.name: The Agate Pattaya Boutique Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Jomtien Second Road · ~300 m to the beach
entries.addr: 413/93-96 Moo 12, Jomtien Second Road, Nong Prue, Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: Scoring 9.4 from 56 reviews — The Agate is a contemporary-Thai boutique resort that delivers the boutique feel without the boutique price. Its 71 rooms come with two pools (one saltwater), a spa, a gym and a hotel tuk-tuk that shuttles guests to Jomtien Beach about 300 m away. Guests consistently praise the friendly staff and the value. Ideal if you want a clean, good-looking place with a pool near the beach without blowing the budget — just note it isn't directly on the sand.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a pool-view room not facing the road for quiet. Groups should take the 50 sqm Sapphire Family room — better value than several small rooms. Check the early-bird rate for booking 60 days ahead.
pros: Scores 9.4 · clean rooms, larger than expected and modern-looking
Friendly, helpful staff — the most-praised part of the stay
Two well-kept, uncrowded pools with a pool bar
Near Jomtien Beach with a tuk-tuk shuttle · great value
cons: Not beachfront — about 300 m by foot or shuttle to the sand
Some furniture is showing its age; smaller rooms feel tight

entries.name: Long Beach Garden Hotel & Pavilions Pattaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Naklua · North Pattaya · on Wong Amat Beach
entries.addr: 499/7 Moo 5, Naklua Road Soi 16, Naklua, Bang Lamung, Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: Scoring 8.6 from 408 reviews — Long Beach Garden is a private-beach resort that's still genuinely cheap in North Pattaya. This large 864-room resort sits on Wong Amat Beach in Naklua, with its own stretch of sand you can walk straight onto and a multi-level outdoor pool kids love. The breakfast buffet is varied (Thai, Indian, European) and over-delivers for the price. Location, beach and value are the strong points — but the resort is ageing and room quality is inconsistent.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a renovated building/zone, or pick a sea-view or pavilion room if budget allows — the difference is clear. Families with young kids love the multi-level pool. Walk to Naklua Market for seafood; Terminal 21 is close.
pros: Private beach you can walk straight onto, cheaper than most beachfront resorts
Attractive multi-level pool kids love, with poolside activities
Varied breakfast — Thai, Indian, European — that beats the price
Near Terminal 21 and Naklua Market · spacious resort grounds
cons: Resort is ageing, some furniture worn, room quality inconsistent
Large grounds with lots of stairs — not ideal for older guests

entries.name: Coco Beach Resort Bangsaen
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bangsaen · Saen Suk · walk to the beach
entries.addr: 20/9 Bangsaen Lang Road 14/3, Saen Suk, Mueang Chon Buri, Bangsaen
entries.storyHtml: Scoring 8.8 (location 9.2, cleanliness 9.1 on Trip.com) — Coco Beach Resort offers a sea-view room by Bangsaen Beach for low four-figure baht. This 45-room, 3-star resort sits on Bangsaen Lang Road, a few minutes' walk from the sand. Among Bangsaen's beachfront stays, it's one of the cheapest that still offers a Deluxe room with a sea view and balcony, plus an outdoor pool and free parking. Real value for a weekend road trip — though the walls are thin and breakfast is à la carte.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pay a little more for one of the roughly 10 sea-view Deluxe rooms — guests agree it's worth it. Light sleepers should ask for a non-adjoining room. Check the breakfast policy before booking, as most is à la carte rather than buffet.
pros: Deluxe sea-view rooms with balconies for low four figures — great value
Walk to Bangsaen Beach, restaurants all around (location score 9.2)
Clean rooms, larger than expected for the price
Free, spacious parking — handy if you drive
cons: Fairly thin walls — you'll hear neighbours at times
Breakfast not included (à la carte) · not a private beach

entries.name: Siam Bayshore Resort Pattaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 South Pattaya · end of Walking Street · by Bali Hai pier
tags: 🚶 End of Walking Street + Bali Hai
entries.addr: 559 Beach Road, South Pattaya, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung, Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: Scoring 8.2 from 379 reviews — Siam Bayshore is a resort hidden in a roughly 8-acre tropical garden at the very end of South Pattaya. The location is rare: right by Walking Street and the Bali Hai pier for Koh Larn. It's a few minutes' walk to the nightlife, but step back inside and the garden walls block out the noise. Open since 1972 and renovated in 2019, it has 270 rooms, two pools, a tennis court and the Lotus Spa — ideal for travellers who want a garden resort in the heart of the South Pattaya action at an accessible price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Specifically request an Executive Deluxe renovated in 2019 — the gap from the older rooms is clear. Ask for a room away from the canal and Walking Street for quiet. You can walk to the Bali Hai pier for the boat to Koh Larn.
pros: Great location — walk to Walking Street and the Bali Hai pier for Koh Larn
Spacious, leafy tropical garden — a real resort feel in the city
Varied breakfast buffet, much praised
Two pools, a tennis court and gym — well-rounded for families
cons: An older resort; some rooms and corners still look dated despite renovation
The canal can smell at low tide · close to the nightlife zone

entries.name: Kalm Bangsaen Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bangsaen · Saen Suk · near Bangsaen Beach
entries.addr: 6 Soi 10, Bangsaen Lang Road, Saen Suk, Mueang Chon Buri, Bangsaen
entries.storyHtml: Scoring 8.3 and ranked #2 of 15 Bangsaen stays on Tripadvisor — Kalm Bangsaen is a boutique hotel with curved architecture you won't find anywhere else in the area. Designed by junnarchitect, the building curves so that nearly half of its 21 rooms face the sea, each with a balcony and bathtub. There's a long saltwater pool, it's a few minutes' walk to Bangsaen Beach and close to Burapha University — ideal for couples or small groups who want a good-looking place at a sensible price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pay a little more for a sea-view room with balcony and bathtub — it's the standout and guests agree it's worth it. Light sleepers should ask for a high floor, as rooms face the beach road. With only 21 rooms, book weekends ahead.
pros: Striking curved design, unlike anything else in Bangsaen
Sea-view rooms with a balcony and bathtub — lovely views
Long saltwater pool, calm atmosphere
Walk to Bangsaen Beach, near Burapha University · friendly staff
cons: Sea-view rooms face the road — some traffic noise on busy weekends
Compact bathrooms · limited indoor common space

entries.name: The Bedrooms Hostel Pattaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Pattaya · 220 m from beach · 3-min walk
entries.addr: 436/49 Moo 9, Beach Road Soi 1, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung, Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: Scoring 9.1 from 247 reviews (location 9.3) — The Bedrooms Hostel is the top-scoring hostel in this guide, a clean bed a 3-minute walk from Pattaya Beach for a few hundred baht. It sits on Beach Road Soi 1, about 220 m from the sand. There are female and male dorms plus private rooms (shared bathrooms), all air-conditioned. What sets it apart from other hostels in the area is free private parking — rare in central Pattaya — plus a shared kitchen and 24-hour reception. Ideal for solo travellers, couples or friends on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Light sleepers should ask for a quieter room away from the road and pack earplugs. Always lock valuables in the safe. Two people are better off in a private double than two dorm beds.
pros: Top-scoring hostel 9.1 · central, 3-min walk to the beach
Clean rooms and shared bathrooms, comfortable beds — beats the price
Free private parking — rare for a city hostel
Shared kitchen, bar and roomy lounge · friendly staff
cons: You'll hear neighbours and the street at night
Rooms are small · even private rooms use shared bathrooms

entries.name: Sindy's Hostel Pattaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pattaya Soi 2 · near Central Marina · ~15-min walk to beach
entries.addr: 78/101 Pattaya Soi 2, Pattaya 2nd Road, Bang Lamung, Pattaya
entries.storyHtml: Scoring 9.1 from 611 reviews on Agoda — Sindy's Hostel offers a clean bed in central Pattaya for a few hundred baht, with free breakfast. It's on Pattaya Soi 2 near Central Marina and Terminal 21, about a 15-minute walk to Pattaya Beach. There are dorm beds and private rooms, all air-conditioned, plus a shared kitchen and staff that international travellers describe as warm. Ideal for solo or budget travellers — though it's an older building with small rooms and some nightlife noise.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Light sleepers should ask for a room not facing the road and pack earplugs for weekends. Make the most of the free breakfast and shared kitchen. Want privacy? Pick a Single/Twin. Ask the desk about boats to Koh Larn.
pros: Central Pattaya, walk to the beach and Central Marina mall
Free breakfast + shared kitchen — handy on a budget
A/C in every room, clean rooms, comfy beds, great value
Friendly, helpful staff · heavily reviewed (611)
cons: Nightlife noise from the surrounding area reaches some rooms
Older building, small rooms, no lift, no pool or on-site parking

entries.name: Bangsaen Heritage Hotel
entries.addr: 50, 54 Bangsaen Beach 1 Road, Saen Suk, Mueang Chonburi, Bangsaen
entries.storyHtml: Bangsaen Heritage is a beach hotel at Bangsaen that gives you a choice of tower rooms or contemporary-Thai garden villas. It sits directly opposite Bangsaen Beach — cross the road and you're at the sea. There's a pool with a slide that kids love and free parking, handy for the drive from Bangkok. The overall score is around 8.1 (Trip.com 8.6, Booking 7.4) — the gap comes down to whether you get a room renovated in 2024. Ideal for families and groups who want an easy beach overnight at Bangsaen on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a Premier room or villa renovated in 2024 — the condition is clearly better. Groups should take the 2-bedroom villa for value. Stop by Nong Mon Market for sticky rice in bamboo and souvenirs on the way home.
pros: Directly opposite Bangsaen Beach — cross the road to the sea
Choice of tower rooms or garden villas, good for bigger groups
Pool with a slide for kids · free parking
Friendly staff · near Nong Mon Market and Khao Sam Muk
cons: Some rooms and villas are still dated and due for refurbishment; quality varies
Garden-villa side has mosquitoes and a longer walk to the centre

adviceTitle: How to pick the right Chonburi & Pattaya hotel for you

advice.head: Tight budget, best value
advice.bodyHtml: → The Bedrooms Hostel Pattaya ฿280, a 3-min walk to the beach with free parking · or Coco Beach Resort Bangsaen ฿1,500 for a sea-view room by Bangsaen Beach

advice.head: Family trip with kids
advice.bodyHtml: → Centara Grand Mirage ฿4,500, in-house waterpark to play all day · or Bangsaen Heritage ฿1,500, garden villas and a pool slide, close to Bangkok

advice.head: Couples trip, calm and quiet
advice.bodyHtml: → Rabbit Resort Pattaya ฿3,500, a Thai village in a garden on Dongtan Beach, with an adults-only pool, scoring 9.4

advice.head: Luxury with a city-centre sea view
advice.bodyHtml: → Hilton Pattaya ฿4,500, a 34-storey tower with sea views in every room, connected to CentralFestival · or The Standard Na Jomtien ฿4,800, design + beach club

advice.head: Want to be on the beach
advice.bodyHtml: → Long Beach Garden ฿1,300, a budget private-beach resort in Naklua · or Centara Grand Mirage ฿4,500, on Wong Amat Beach

advice.head: Design with character
advice.bodyHtml: → The Standard, Pattaya Na Jomtien ฿4,800, 1960s-style design · or Kalm Bangsaen ฿1,800, a curved-architecture boutique with sea views

advice.head: Stay in the heart of the action
advice.bodyHtml: → Siam Bayshore Resort ฿2,800, a garden resort at the end of Walking Street · or Sindy's Hostel ฿390, central Pattaya with free breakfast

advice.head: Weekend drive to Bangsaen
advice.bodyHtml: → Coco Beach Resort Bangsaen ฿1,500, sea-view rooms with free parking · or Kalm Bangsaen ฿1,800, a design boutique near the beach

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate and change by date and season. Always check live rates and compare 3 sites before booking. Over Thai and Chinese long weekends and in high season (Nov–Feb), prices rise and rooms sell out fast — book 1–2 weeks ahead or more. Chonburi & Pattaya have no metro; get around by songthaew, Grab or your own car. From Bangkok it's roughly 1.5–2 hours to Pattaya and 1.5 hours to Bangsaen. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — Common questions about Chonburi & Pattaya hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in around Chonburi & Pattaya?
faq.a: It depends on your style. Central Pattaya suits people who want convenience — next to the malls and beach, with nightlife (Hilton, The Bedrooms, Sindy's, Siam Bayshore). Naklua–Wong Amat in North Pattaya is quieter and cleaner, great for families (Centara Grand Mirage, Long Beach Garden). Jomtien–Na Jomtien has calm beaches and clear water for relaxing (Rabbit Resort, The Standard, The Agate). Bangsaen is the sea nearest Bangkok, ideal for a weekend road trip (Coco Beach, Kalm Bangsaen, Bangsaen Heritage).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Chonburi & Pattaya hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: central hostels start around ฿280–850/night; 3–4 star beachfront resorts and hotels around ฿1,300–3,500; boutique and 4–5 star luxury around ฿3,500–4,800, with suites higher. Over long weekends, festivals and high season (Nov–Feb) prices can run well above normal, especially for beachfront hotels.

faq.q: ❓ Pattaya or Bangsaen — which should I choose?
faq.a: Pattaya has the fullest range of accommodation, beaches, activities, malls and nightlife, best for multi-night stays. Bangsaen, in Chonburi city, is closer to Bangkok (about 1.5 hours by car) and ideal for an easy weekend drive — the water there is better for relaxing on the beach than serious swimming. Choose Pattaya for activities and sights; choose Bangsaen for closeness and speed.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Chonburi & Pattaya hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion at any given time, so always compare all three before booking — every review page in this guide has price-comparison links, which can save you several hundred baht a night.

faq.q: ❓ Which hotels are directly on the beach so I can walk to the sea?
faq.a: Directly beachfront options: Centara Grand Mirage and Long Beach Garden on Wong Amat Beach in North Pattaya; Rabbit Resort on Dongtan Beach, Jomtien; and The Standard, Pattaya Na Jomtien on Na Jomtien Beach with a private beach. In Bangsaen most stays are opposite/walking distance to a public beach rather than on private sand.

faq.q: ❓ How do I get from Bangkok to Chonburi & Pattaya, and how long does it take?
faq.a: Driving from Bangkok takes about 1.5 hours to Bangsaen and 1.5–2 hours to Pattaya via the motorway. Vans and buses run from Ekkamai/Mo Chit to Pattaya all day. If you fly into U-Tapao Airport (UTP), it's about 45 min to Pattaya. Locally, songthaew (red baht-bus), Grab or your own car are easiest.
